meta.homeTitle: Create a lasting online memorial | missingu.org
meta.homeDescription: MissingU is a calm, private place to remember someone: build an online memorial, share a life story, add photos, light a candle, and let family and friends gather in memory.

help.title: Help centre
help.intro: Answers to the questions families ask most.
help.q1: How do I create a memorial page?
help.a1: On the home page, tap “Create a memorial”, enter the name and dates and upload a portrait. You can also start from “Publish an obituary”, which sets up the memorial for you.
help.q2: Why can't others find my page in search or on the home page?
help.a2: A new page is a draft at first. Open it and tap “Publish”, and set visibility to “Public”. Only then is it searchable and shown in “Recently remembered” on its channel's home page (for a month after publishing).
help.q3: How do I find a memorial?
help.a3: Search the person's name from the home page or the search box, or enter the 8-digit memorial number to open the page directly.
help.q4: Who can see my memorial? Can I make it private?
help.a4: Yes. On the manage page you can set the visibility: Public, Unlisted (kept out of search), or Invite-only.
help.q5: What's the difference between offerings, donations to the family, and supporting the platform?
help.a5: Incense is free — a gesture of remembrance. Candles, wreaths and donations are gifts to the family. “Support the platform” in the footer funds the running of the site and does not go to any family.
help.q6: Is a memorial free forever? How do I delete it?
help.a6: Creating and visiting a memorial is free forever, with no charge to families. To remove one, open the manage page and request deletion.

obituaryGuide.title: How to write an obituary: format, elements and a template
obituaryGuide.lead: An obituary announces a death to family, friends and community and shares the funeral or memorial arrangements. This guide covers the standard format and the elements to include, with a template you can adapt in minutes.
obituaryGuide.whatBody: An obituary is a formal notice published by the family that gives the person's name and date of death and tells relatives and friends when and where the farewell, memorial service or burial will take place. The tone is dignified and the content concise and accurate.
obituaryGuide.formatIntro: A complete obituary usually includes these elements:
obituaryGuide.formatItems:
Heading: usually the word “Obituary”, or “Obituary of [Name]”
The deceased: full name, dates of birth and death, age
The passing: when and (optionally) how they died
A brief life note: role or main achievements (optional)
Arrangements: date and place of the farewell, service or burial
Signature: the family or funeral committee, and the date of notice
obituaryGuide.templateNote: Replace the bracketed details with the real information:
obituaryGuide.template:
IN LOVING MEMORY
[Full name], aged [age], of [city], passed away peacefully on [date].
He/She is lovingly remembered by [family members].
A memorial service will be held at [time] on [date] at [place].
The family thanks everyone for their kindness and support.
— The [surname] family
obituaryGuide.onlineBody: Beyond print, many families now publish an online obituary: it can carry a portrait, be shared instantly, and let distant relatives pay their respects online. On missingu.org you can publish an obituary for free and get a permanent memorial page and a shareable poster.
obituaryGuide.tipsItems:
Get names, dates, times and places exactly right
Keep the tone dignified and concise; avoid slang
Use a title that matches the writer (e.g. “father”, “mother”)
Note any wake, flowers or donation wishes
Have the family check every detail before publishing
obituaryGuide.ctaTitle: Publish an obituary free on missingu.org
